public_rationale: The provider half largely holds. In April 2026 Anthropic stopped letting flat-rate Claude plans power third-party agent tools such as OpenClaw. On June 1 GitHub moved every Copilot plan to usage-based billing. But Anthropic paused a wider change on June 15, so agent use kept drawing on subscriptions, which tempers this half. The customer half does not hold in aggregate. Anthropic's S-1 shows $16.3 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026, against $4.6 billion in all of 2025. The NYT says most of that revenue is companies paying for the tokens their workers use. Some firms (Uber, Meta, Walmart) did cap spending. But customers as a whole were paying per token far more than before.
limitations: Revenue is an indirect measure of willingness to pay.
The usage-based share of Anthropic revenue is not quantified in the cited sources.
Only a few providers are examined.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM providers no longer want to offer all-you-can-eat pricing and customers no longer want to pay per-token a la carte.

statement.excerpt: The LLM providers no longer want to offer all-you-can-eat and customers no longer want to pay for a la carte.
statement.document_title: Breaking news, and how the end might begin

from_speaker: The LLM providers no longer want to offer all-you-can-eat
customers no longer want to pay for a la carte
our_interpretation: This is two claims. (a) Providers: major LLM and AI-tool providers were moving away from flat-rate plans that covered heavy or agent use. (b) Customers: customers were resisting usage-based (per-token) pricing, shown by falling or stalling usage-based spending.
Target period is April to June 2026: the recent pricing changes and spending up to the end of the quarter in which the post appeared.
Customer reluctance is judged from total spending by customers at the leading usage-based provider, alongside reports of individual firms capping spend.
criteria.support_condition: (a) Major providers restricted or ended flat-rate access for heavy or agent use in April–June 2026, and (b) usage-based spending fell or stalled, or customers widely refused metered pricing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: (a) Providers kept or expanded flat-rate access, or (b) customer spending on usage-based AI kept rising sharply in the period.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic has blocked Claude Pro and Max subscribers from using their flat-rate plans with third-party AI agent frameworks, starting with OpenClaw.
evidence.explanation: A major provider withdrew flat-rate access for heavy agent use. This supports the provider half.

evidence.excerpt: As of June 1, all Copilot plans bill based on GitHub AI Credits consumed.
evidence.locator: section 'Usage-based billing is active for all Copilot plans'
evidence.explanation: A major AI coding provider moved every plan to metered billing. This supports the provider half.

evidence.excerpt: For now, nothing changes. The Agent SDK, claude -p, and third-party apps still draw from regular subscription limits, Anthropic says.
evidence.explanation: Anthropic dropped its planned move of agent use off subscriptions, citing competitive pressure. This partly cuts against the provider half.

evidence.excerpt: said it generated $16.3 billion in revenue in the six-month period that ended in June, more than the $4.6 billion the company saw in all of 2025.
evidence.explanation: Customer spending at the leading LLM provider, mostly per-token enterprise spending, more than tripled versus all of 2025 in just six months. This contradicts the claim that customers no longer want to pay a la carte.

evidence.excerpt: But the bulk of the revenue comes from offering tools to companies like Meta, Shopify and Amazon, which pay not only subscription fees but for the tokens used by their tens of thousands of workers.
evidence.publisher: The Star (syndicating The New York Times)
evidence.explanation: Shows that most AI lab revenue is per-token spending, which links revenue growth to customers' willingness to pay a la carte. The same article reports some firms capping that spending.
